metadata.title: The $1.65T That 'Disappeared': Hyperscaler Shadow Borrowing for AI Data Centers

conclusion: SV101's Chen Xi maps $1.65T of US top-five data-center debt that BIS would call shadow borrowing — Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Oracle hiding leverage so the balance sheet stays 'clean.' Buybacks collapsed from $48B in 2021 Q4 to $4.6B in 2026 Q1. Epoch: opex cash +23%/yr vs capex +70%, crossing in 2026 Q3; Morgan Stanley needs $1.5T of external capital by 2028 on $2.9T of DC spend. Oracle is the stressed name (capex $21.2B→$55.7B, S&P BBB to BBB-). Meta's Hyperion SPV borrowed $27.3B and put $2.37B on Meta's books — then pays 6.581% vs ~5.5% unsecured to keep it off-balance-sheet.
background: Chen Xi explainer after flipping hyperscaler filings. Five hide-the-debt tools, Blue Owl's SaaS-to-DC pivot after a 40% redemption / <15% payout, and whether this is a subprime rhyme. Microsoft is the exception: no public issuance since 2024 and falling total debt. Prospectuses say 'general corporate purposes,' never 'data center.'
important_facts: Cash vs build: five hyperscalers' combined buybacks $48B (2021 Q4 peak) → $12.9B last year Q4 → $4.6B 2026 Q1, down ~90%. Only Microsoft still buying; Google stopped in Q1; Meta three straight zero quarters; Oracle < $100M last FY; Amazon none since mid-2022. Epoch (June): operating cash +~23%/yr vs capex +~70%, lines cross 2026 Q3 — 'collectively broke' before 2027 if the slope holds. Morgan Stanley: $2.9T global DC capex through 2028, $1.4T from hyperscaler cash, $1.5T external. Bond issuance $28B/yr 2020–24 → $108.3B in 2025 → almost $200B YTD through July 2026 (~6× the old annual). Microsoft issued no public debt 2024–now. Filings avoid the words data center / AI — Meta's $30B deal and Oracle's 2026-02 print say general corporate purposes (Oracle even said dividends and buybacks the next day).

Why not just sell more public bonds: (1) oversubscription thinned — Amazon 5.3× (Nov) to 1.6× (2026-07) as hundreds of billions stacked in one window; (2) new-issue concession 2.25 bp median 2025 → 12 bp 2026, Amazon's long tranche +18–21 bp; (3) the 'cash machine, no debt, buybacks' compact with quality funds breaks; (4) on-balance-sheet debt hits ratings. Oracle capex $21.2B → $55.7B in a year; S&P BBB → BBB- in July, one notch from junk, which can lose insurers/pensions. They want more money, longer tenor (DC payback 10–20 years), and off-balance-sheet optics — public IG cannot deliver all three.

Private credit fills the hole after SaaS souring: Blue Owl fund saw 40% redemption two straight quarters and paid <15%; stock $24 → $9. BIS (July): 60% of PC loans to SaaS borrowers already borrowed from 7+ lenders vs <10% a decade ago. Software stocks ~−40% from 2025-09 highs even as M365 growth 15%→19%. DC securities $1.3B (2022) → $30–40B, ~20×. Case: Meta Hyperion — $27.3B at Beignet Investor / Laidley LLC in Louisiana, Blue Owl OSNL on top, Delaware shells in <6 weeks, no SEC prospectus. Blue Owl 63% of Beignet Investor and 80% of the PropCo; Meta's 20% is the $2.37B on its books, so $27.29B at 6.581% to 2049-05 stays off-balance-sheet. Pelican Leap lease from 2029, 4-year initial term, residual guarantee ~$28B. Same-tenor Meta unsecured ~5.5% — ~$300M extra interest/year for the clean sheet. July Sopaipilla (El Paso) $12.5B at 7.534% to 2048, BlackRock in the 80% seat; two Meta DC deals ~$40B in under a year.

mental_model.name: Shadow Borrowing × Rating Cliff × Residual Guarantee
mental_model.components: Hyperscalers need more cash, longer tenor, and a clean consolidated sheet. Public IG is slower, dearer, and fully on-balance-sheet — so SPV + lease + residual guarantee moves $27B off Meta while Meta still pays. Price of cleanliness is ~100 bp (5.5% vs 6.581%) and a one-notch haircut (AA- name, A+ paper). Oracle is the on-balance-sheet warning: capex jump plus BBB-. Blue Owl is recycling SaaS credit risk into DC paper after a redemption freeze. Buyback collapse is the real-economy tell that FCF is staying inside the building.
mental_model.application: ORCL is the stressed public print (rating, capex, prospectus mismatch). META's Hyperion/Sopaipilla stack is hidden leverage — add lease + residual to the model even if GAAP is clean. MSFT's no-issue / still-buyback tape is the quality exception. AMZN concession and 1.6× books show the public window is tiring. Do not treat $1.65T as 'disappeared'; it is Meta-backed and Blue Owl / BlackRock-held. A SaaS-loan maturity wall (11% by 2027, 20% by 2028) is why this paper exists.

key_insights.question: Where did Hyperion's $27B go?
key_insights.answer: Delaware Beignet SPVs, 80/20 with Blue Owl, lease + ~$28B residual on Meta. Off-balance-sheet, still Meta's obligation.

key_insights.view: Public IG cannot give all three.
key_insights.question: What do hyperscalers want?
key_insights.answer: More money, 10–20 year tenor, and a clean sheet. That is why they pay 6.581% instead of 5.5%.

key_insights.view: Oracle is already on the cliff.
key_insights.question: Who is the stressed name?
key_insights.answer: Capex $21.2B→$55.7B and S&P BBB→BBB-. Microsoft is the exception that has not issued.

top_investment_implications.thesis: On-balance-sheet capex jump and BBB- print; one notch from losing IG buyers — medium
Hyperion residual still Meta's; extra ~$300M/yr interest is the price of a clean sheet, not free leverage — low
Only name still buying back and issuing no public debt 2024–now — the quality exception on this tape — medium
